q-6499: Correct answer: A. Every motorcycle must have a working device for giving a sound signal, because it serves to warn other road users. A fire extinguisher and a first-aid kit are not part of its compulsory equipment.
q-6500: Correct answer: C. A two-wheeled motorcycle faster than 100 km/h must have at least two exterior mirrors, because at such speeds watching the road behind the vehicle is particularly important. A fire extinguisher and a triangle are not required for it.
q-6501: Correct answer: C. A motorcycle does not have to be fitted with hazard lights, but fitting them is allowed. If the vehicle has them, the rider uses them in situations where others must be warned of a danger or of a stop in a dangerous place.
q-6502: Correct answer: B. A motorcycle must have a rear reflector of a shape other than a triangle. Triangular reflectors are reserved for trailers, so that it can be seen from afar that a combination is being towed behind the vehicle.
q-6503: Correct answer: B. The minimum permitted tread depth is 1.6 mm; below that value the tyre loses its ability to clear water and the vehicle may not be admitted to traffic. The lower values in the answers are not permitted.
q-6504: Correct answer: B. A motorcycle with a sidecar is a multi-track vehicle, so it must carry a warning triangle for marking a vehicle immobilised on the road. A first-aid kit and a fire extinguisher are not compulsory for it.
q-6507: Correct answer: B. A motorcyclist must wear a protective helmet, and the only exception concerns a motorcycle factory-fitted with seat belts, where the vehicle's structure provides the protection. A sidecar alone does not release you from this duty.
q-6508: Correct answer: A. A moped must have a working device for giving a sound signal, which allows other road users to be warned. A fire extinguisher and a first-aid kit are not part of its compulsory equipment.
q-6509: Correct answer: B. A moped tyre without a wear indicator must have a tread pattern at least 1.6 mm deep. Shallower tread does not clear water from under the wheel and clearly lengthens the braking distance on a wet surface.
q-6510: Correct answer: C. A moped must have at least one rear-view mirror on the left side, giving the rider a view of the road behind the vehicle. A warning triangle and a fire extinguisher belong to a car's equipment, not a two-wheeler's.
q-6512: Correct answer: B. The compulsory equipment of a moped includes a rear reflector of a shape other than a triangle. The triangular reflector is reserved for trailers, so placing one on a moped would mislead other drivers.
q-6513: Correct answer: C. A moped must have a white light at the front, with which it lights the road and is visible after dusk and in conditions of reduced clarity of the air. A fire extinguisher and a warning triangle are not required for it.
q-6548: Correct answer: C. Mirrors do not show the whole area to the side and behind, so before changing lane a glance in the mirrors is combined with a brief turn of the head. Turning the head alone, in turn, removes control over what is happening ahead.
q-6556: Correct answer: B. In a typical sequential motorcycle gearbox, neutral lies between first and second gear, at half the lever's travel. That is why before stopping it is selected with a gentle upward movement from first, and its engagement is confirmed by the indicator light.
q-6559: Correct answer: B. ABS does not let the wheels lock, so the front wheel keeps rolling and the motorcycle stays steerable — you can steer round an obstacle without easing off the brake. On loose or uneven ground, however, the braking distance with ABS can be longer.
q-6621: Correct answer: B. Excessive chain slack must be removed as soon as it is found, because a loose chain can come off or lock the rear wheel. The manufacturer's recommendations set the check intervals but do not excuse you from reacting to a fault you have noticed.
q-6624: Correct answer: A. A lit oil-pressure light means there is no proper lubrication, and keeping the engine running risks seizing it. Pull over to a safe place, switch off the engine and establish the cause before continuing.
q-6626: Correct answer: C. Too low a pressure deforms the tyre, so its tread does not sit evenly on the surface and grip falls. The vehicle responds more sluggishly to the handlebars, and the tyre wears and overheats faster.
q-6628: Correct answer: C. Sharp acceleration puts large, jerky forces on the chain, which stretch its links and wear the sprockets faster. So with such a riding style the tension must be checked and adjusted more often than usual.
q-6629: Correct answer: C. Too low a pressure deforms the tyre, so its tread does not sit evenly on the surface and grip falls. The vehicle responds more sluggishly to the handlebars, and the tyre wears and overheats faster.
q-6664: Correct answer: B. An agricultural tractor must have at least two exterior mirrors — on the left and on the right — because a towed machine or trailer blocks the view behind. An interior mirror is not required in such a vehicle.
q-6675: Correct answer: B. Grip arises at the contact of tyre and surface, so it depends above all on whether that is asphalt, concrete, cobbles or an unmade road. Engine power and the state of the steering affect driving but do not create grip.
q-6676: Correct answer: A. Less grip means less force the wheels can pass to the surface, so the vehicle needs a longer stretch to stop. Braking is still possible, but requires earlier and gentler use of the brake.
q-6710: Correct answer: B. The lubrication light responds to oil pressure and comes on when it falls below the permissible level. You must then stop the vehicle immediately and switch off the engine, because it risks seizing. It does not tell you when to change the oil or about the filter.
q-6716: Correct answer: B. The correct oil level lies between the MIN and MAX marks. Below MIN there is not enough oil; above MAX the excess foams and loads the seals. The measurement is taken with a dipstick wiped dry, on level ground.
q-6717: Correct answer: A. A level above the MAX mark is incorrect: excess oil foams, and pressure and the load on the seals rise. A reading between MIN and MAX, including just above MIN, is considered correct.
q-6718: Correct answer: C. A level below the MIN mark is incorrect — there is too little oil, lubrication and cooling of the parts deteriorate, and the engine risks seizing. A reading between MIN and MAX, including just below MAX, is correct.
q-6719: Correct answer: B. A tractor with the oil level below the MIN mark may not be operated — lubrication is insufficient and the engine can seize in a short time. The oil must be topped up before moving off, even before driving to the workshop.
q-6720: Correct answer: B. The position-light indicator is a green symbol of two lamps emitting light to the sides; in the set it corresponds to variant B. The green colour of indicator lights signals a correctly working, switched-on function.
q-6721: Correct answer: C. The main-beam indicator shines blue and has a headlamp symbol with straight, horizontal rays; variant C corresponds to it. Dipped headlights are marked by a symbol with rays pointing diagonally downwards.
q-6722: Correct answer: A. Hazard lights in use are signalled by a red triangle symbol flashing together with all the indicators; variant A corresponds to it. Hazard lights are used when stopped because of a breakdown and when creating a danger.
q-6724: Correct answer: B. Too low an engine oil level is signalled by a red light with an oil-can symbol and a drop; in the set variant B corresponds to it. When it comes on, the engine should be switched off and the oil level checked with the dipstick.
q-6725: Correct answer: C. An applied emergency brake lever is signalled by a red light with an exclamation mark or the letter P in a circle; in the set that is variant C. Driving with the brake applied overheats and destroys the brake mechanisms.
q-6749: Correct answer: B. ABS does not let the wheels lock under braking, so the wheels keep rolling and the vehicle stays steerable. It does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions — on gravel or fresh snow it can even lengthen it.
q-6786: Correct answer: B. The exterior mirrors are set to take in the area behind the vehicle and a narrow strip of your own side as a reference point. This setting reduces the blind spot when changing lane and turning, although it does not eliminate it entirely.
q-6790: Correct answer: A. In emergency braking the brake and clutch pedals are pressed hard and held until the vehicle stops, despite vibration and pulsing of the pedal — that is the normal working of the system. Easing the pressure or pumping the brake lengthens the braking distance and is not needed.
q-6818: Correct answer: B. A tread depth below 1.6 mm means excessive tyre wear and disqualifies the tyre. Shallow tread does not clear water from under the wheel, so the risk of aquaplaning grows and the braking distance on a wet surface clearly lengthens.
q-6854: Correct answer: A. A school bus must have a sound signal warning the surroundings that it is reversing, because there is a large area behind the vehicle invisible to the driver, and children are nearby. Cones or a separate cab are not required equipment.
q-6855: Correct answer: C. A city bus must have an interior mirror letting the driver watch the inside of the vehicle, especially the area by the doors. Thanks to it the driver sees passengers getting on and off and can close the doors and move off safely.
q-6856: Correct answer: C. Before moving off, the driver must check that access to the emergency exits is clear and that neither luggage nor standing passengers block them. This duty does not depend on the number of seats in the bus.
q-6858: Correct answer: A. The belt protects only when it is fastened and correctly positioned: the lap part low across the hips, the shoulder part across the middle of the collarbone, without slack and without a twist in the webbing. A loose belt or webbing across the neck increases the risk of serious injury.
q-6880: Correct answer: A. On a dry road grip is decided above all by the type of surface — asphalt, paving or concrete give different coefficients of friction. Engine power and the state of the steering affect the vehicle's handling but not grip itself.
q-6896: Correct answer: B. The exterior mirrors should take in the area behind the vehicle and a narrow strip of your own side as a reference point. In a long bus this setting is essential when changing lane and turning, because it reduces the extensive blind spot.
q-6898: Correct answer: B. A bus is accelerated most effectively by changing gear within the green band of the rev counter, that is, where the engine has the greatest torque and the lowest fuel consumption. Revving the engine to the maximum or running in the red band only damages it.
q-6921: Correct answer: B. The vehicle is raised with the jack just enough to leave a gap under the tyre sufficient to fit the good wheel. The engine should be off and the parking brake applied — releasing it risks the vehicle slipping off the jack.
q-6922: Correct answer: A. The jack is placed only at the point indicated by the manufacturer, because only there does the structure bear the vehicle's weight. The wheel bolts, in turn, are tightened to the recommended torque — too much force can stretch them or damage the thread.
q-6935: Correct answer: A. On a motorway and an expressway the warning triangle is placed 100 m behind the vehicle, because high speeds require earlier warning of approaching traffic. Shorter distances apply to other roads.
q-7075: Correct answer: C. The sander is used whenever the rail is slippery, regardless of whether the cause is leaves, moisture, frost or snow. Sand increases grip, makes starting easier and shortens the braking distance.
q-7115: Correct answer: C. Sand applied under the wheels increases grip at the contact of wheel and rail and shortens the braking distance, so it is used in sudden emergency braking. Using the sanders at every braking is unnecessary and quickly empties the hoppers.
q-7116: Correct answer: C. Only dry sand intended for the purpose may be put into the sanders, and it is topped up at the nearest terminus. Gravel would damage the device and the track, and stopping the set on the route would block traffic.
q-7177: Correct answer: A. An agricultural tractor must be equipped with a fire extinguisher regardless of whether it is towing a trailer. The extinguisher should be placed in an easily accessible place and be in working order with a current inspection.
q-7210: Correct answer: B. A bus for which a speed of 100 km/h is permitted must be equipped with a first-aid kit. The 6 mm tread and three-point belts on all seats mentioned in the other answers are not among those requirements.
q-7211: Correct answer: A. The type-approved limiter fitted in a bus is set so that the vehicle cannot exceed 100 km/h. The device limits the fuel supply and works independently of the limit in force on the road in question.
q-7536: Correct answer: B. A bus longer than 6 metres must be equipped with two fire extinguishers: one near the driver's seat, the other in the passenger area. Shorter buses need only one extinguisher.
q-7537: Correct answer: A. A bus no longer than 6 metres must be equipped with at least one fire extinguisher. Longer buses require more of them, and the extinguisher itself must be in working order, secured and easily accessible.
q-7553: Correct answer: A. Too high a pressure reduces the tyre's contact area with the surface, so grip and braking effectiveness fall. The motorcycle becomes harsher, absorbs bumps worse and loses contact with the road more easily.
q-7554: Correct answer: B. With too low a pressure the tyre deforms, the motorcycle holds its line worse and responds sluggishly to the handlebars, especially in curves. The tyre additionally overheats and wears faster.
q-7588: Correct answer: C. A motorcyclist and the passenger carried must wear a protective helmet meeting the applicable technical requirements. The exception is a vehicle factory-fitted with seat belts, where the vehicle's structure and a fastened belt provide the protection.
q-7593: Correct answer: C. The duty of a moped rider and the passenger carried to wear a protective helmet applies regardless of the type of road and its surface. The sign shown in the material does not release you from this duty, because it concerns the traffic arrangement, not the rider's equipment.
q-7604: Correct answer: B. In a well-set exterior mirror you can see a narrow strip of the vehicle's side, which gives a reference point, and the space behind the vehicle on the same side. Without a piece of your own body it is hard to judge the distance of vehicles behind.
q-7630: Correct answer: C. Grip arises at the contact of tyre and carriageway, so it depends on what the surface is made of and what state it is in — dry, wet, muddy or icy. Neither engine power nor a passenger's mass decides it.
q-7661: Correct answer: C. A bus must be equipped with a warning triangle, with which a vehicle immobilised on the road is marked. The rules do not, however, oblige a city bus to carry a spare wheel or a first-aid kit.
q-7662: Correct answer: C. The belt webbing must lie against the body below the neck: across the middle of the collarbone, the chest and low across the hips. A belt resting on the neck risks serious injury under harsh braking, and a loose one will not hold the body in the seat.
q-7678: Correct answer: B. Over numerous bumps the wheels momentarily lose contact with the surface, and the ABS system reads this as locking and reduces the braking force. The braking distance grows, so on a bumpy road you must drive slower.
q-7680: Correct answer: C. A narrow strip of the bus's side must be visible in the mirror as a reference point, together with the space behind the vehicle on the same side. This lets you judge the distance of vehicles behind and change lane safely.
q-7697: Correct answer: B. The light indicated signals that the emergency brake lever remains applied. Before moving off it must be fully released, because driving with the brake acting overheats the linings and increases fuel consumption.
q-7731: Correct answer: C. Grip is decided above all by the type and state of the surface — dry, wet, icy or muddy asphalt behaves differently. Tyre size and engine power do not in themselves create grip.
q-7765: Correct answer: A. Before raising the bus with a jack, chocks are placed under the opposite wheel so that the vehicle does not move. The parking brake stays applied, and the gearbox is not put into neutral.
q-7859: Correct answer: B. The red band of the rev counter is the range of revs above the value permitted by the manufacturer. Prolonged driving in that range overloads and overheats the engine, leading to damage, and fuel consumption rises as well.
q-8857: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle with ABS you brake with firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal — the system itself prevents the wheels from locking and keeps the vehicle steerable. Pumping the brake is used in vehicles without ABS.
q-10811: Correct answer: B. Exempt from the duty to fasten seat belts is, among others, a child under 3 carried in a bus. A taxi driver while carrying a passenger and a woman who is visibly pregnant are exempt from this duty, so the other answers are wrong.
q-11437: Correct answer: B. The airbag is a system supplementing the belts, not a replacement for them. Without belts fastened, the body moves forward and meets the inflating airbag, which risks serious injury to the head or spine.
q-11450: Correct answer: C. Grip is decided above all by the type and state of the surface — dry, wet, icy or muddy asphalt behaves differently. Tyre size and engine power do not in themselves create grip.
q-11453: Correct answer: B. An over-inflated tyre touches the carriageway with a smaller area, so grip falls and the braking distance grows. Pressure is set according to the manufacturer's recommendations and the vehicle's current load.
q-11467: Correct answer: B. The green band of the rev counter marks the range of most favourable torque, so changing gear within it gives the best acceleration. Revving the engine to the maximum or entering the red band only increases fuel consumption and the load on the mechanisms.
q-11471: Correct answer: C. ABS does not let the wheels lock, so the tyres keep their lateral force and the vehicle still responds to the steering during emergency braking. The system does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions — on gravel or snow it can even be longer.
q-11472: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle with ABS you brake with full force, because the system makes sure the wheels do not lock, and the pressed clutch prevents the engine from stalling. Pulsing and gradually increasing the pedal pressure only lengthen the braking distance.
q-11483: Correct answer: A. Heavy machines must be immobilised with lashings and chocks, because under braking enormous inertial forces act on them. An applied parking brake alone will not hold the machine, and the length of the route is of no significance here.
q-11489: Correct answer: A. A fault in the anti-lock system is signalled by a warning light on the dashboard that comes on and does not go out. The brakes still work, but without protection against the wheels locking, so on a slippery surface you must brake more carefully.
q-11492: Correct answer: B. The minimum permitted tread depth is 1.6 mm. Shallower tread clears water from under the wheel less well and loses grip abruptly, especially on a wet surface.
q-11493: Correct answer: A. A red coolant temperature light means the engine is overheating. Stop the vehicle as quickly and safely as possible and switch off the engine, because driving on risks serious damage to it.
q-11494: Correct answer: A. A red oil-pressure light means the engine's lubrication is not assured. Stop the vehicle immediately and safely and switch off the engine, because running without oil pressure destroys it in a very short time.
q-2686: Correct answer: A. Roadside checks, including checking the driver's documents, are carried out by a police officer, and within their powers also by a municipal guard. A tram driver is the driver of a vehicle, so they are subject to such checks under the general rules.
q-4111: Correct answer: B. The sound signal is compulsory equipment — without it the tram driver cannot warn a pedestrian or a driver of the approaching car. A tram with a faulty bell may not be taken out on the route, and an entry in the documents does not change that.
q-6400: Correct answer: B. A child up to 6 years old may be carried in a quadricycle only when the speed does not exceed 40 km/h. The restriction follows from the modest protection such a vehicle gives, so the driving must be calm, without sudden manoeuvres.
q-6422: Correct answer: C. An invalid driving licence gives no entitlement to drive any vehicle covered by the category in question, a quadricycle included, and there is no grace period here. The document must be replaced before its validity expires.
q-6426: Correct answer: A. The state after alcohol consumption begins at 0.2‰ in the blood, and from that value driving a vehicle is prohibited. The lower readings given in the other answers do not mark the threshold adopted in the rules.
q-6430: Correct answer: B. Category B1 covers quadricycles, that is, light motor vehicles of limited unladen mass. A motorcycle with a sidecar belongs to a motorcycle category, and a heavier motor vehicle requires category B.
q-6431: Correct answer: B. A category B1 entitlement also covers driving a moped, because it is a lighter and slower vehicle than those covered by that category. A car requires category B, and an agricultural tractor — category T.
q-6531: Correct answer: A. The distance between moving columns of mopeds may not be less than 200 m. That gap lets other drivers overtake a single column and return safely to their lane.
q-6567: Correct answer: A. The ban on carrying a person after alcohol consumption concerns a two-wheeler, because a passenger on the pillion seat has a share in the vehicle's balance. In a sidecar such a person does not affect the stability of the outfit, so carrying them is permitted.
q-6576: Correct answer: A. A person after alcohol consumption may not be carried on a moped in any circumstances. A passenger on a two-wheeler shares in keeping the balance, and impaired coordination risks the vehicle falling over; reducing speed does not lift this ban.
q-6584: Correct answer: C. A person after alcohol consumption may not be carried on a two-wheeled motorcycle. The rider's own assessment does not replace this ban, and a speed limit does not lift it — a passenger with impaired coordination can tip the vehicle at the worst moment.
q-6585: Correct answer: A. An intoxicated person may not be carried on a two-wheeled motorcycle in any variant. Such a passenger does not control their own movements and shifts their body weight independently of the rider, which risks the vehicle falling over.
q-6586: Correct answer: A. An intoxicated person may not be carried on a moped. The balance of a two-wheeler also depends on the passenger, and their unpredictable movements can topple the vehicle; neither slow riding nor the rider's own judgement lifts this ban.
q-6592: Correct answer: A. The owner notifies the starosta of the acquisition of a registered motorcycle within 30 days of the purchase. The notification updates the data in the register, so that responsibility for the vehicle passes to the new owner.
q-6594: Correct answer: C. A change of circumstances requiring the data in the registration document to be corrected is reported to the starosta within 30 days. This concerns, for example, a change of the owner's address or structural changes to the vehicle.
q-6599: Correct answer: A. Category A entitles you to drive any motorcycle, including a combination of a motorcycle and a sidecar. A quadricycle and a slow-moving vehicle require other entitlements, so category A alone is not enough to drive them.
q-6604: Correct answer: A. Category A1 covers three-wheeled motorcycles with a power not exceeding 15 kW. A quadricycle with an unladen mass of 550 kg and a slow-moving vehicle do not fall within these entitlements and require another category of driving licence.
q-6605: Correct answer: A. A category A1 driving licence allows you to ride a motorcycle with an engine capacity of up to 125 cm³. A motorcycle with a larger capacity requires category A2 or A, depending on its power and power-to-weight ratio.
q-6606: Correct answer: C. Every driving-licence category covering motorcycles also confers the entitlement to ride a moped, so a holder of category A1 may ride a moped. A slow-moving vehicle and any quadricycle remain outside these entitlements.
q-6608: Correct answer: A. Category A2 includes the entitlements of category A1, and therefore also a three-wheeled motorcycle with a power not exceeding 15 kW. A quadricycle with an unladen mass of 550 kg and a slow-moving vehicle require entirely different categories.
q-6609: Correct answer: A. Category A2 allows you to ride a motorcycle with a power of up to 35 kW, with the power-to-unladen-mass ratio also limited. A more powerful motorcycle requires full category A.
q-6610: Correct answer: C. Motorcycle entitlements also cover riding a moped, so a holder of category A2 may ride a moped. A slow-moving vehicle and any quadricycle remain outside the scope of this category.
q-6613: Correct answer: C. Category AM entitles you to drive a moped and a light quadricycle, that is, a vehicle of small unladen mass and limited power. A three-wheeled motorcycle and the other quadricycles require higher categories.
q-6614: Correct answer: B. An electrically powered moped may have a motor with a power of no more than 4 kW. A vehicle with a more powerful motor is no longer a moped, and category AM is not enough to drive it.
q-6617: Correct answer: B. Category AM covers a moped and a light quadricycle. A three-wheeled motorcycle and any quadricycle without mass and power limits go beyond these entitlements and require a higher category of driving licence.
q-6618: Correct answer: B. Category AM allows you to drive a light quadricycle and, among scooters, only those that meet the conditions for a moped. A scooter of larger capacity or power and a three-wheeled motorcycle require a motorcycle category.
q-6662: Correct answer: A. A vehicle carrying out cleaning work on the road, travelling with its yellow flashing light on and taking special care, may also move off the carriageway. The ban on reversing on a motorway and the duty to give way to trams still apply.
q-6708: Correct answer: C. Category T entitles you to drive an agricultural tractor, also with trailers, and a slow-moving vehicle. A car requires category B, and a motorcycle the appropriate motorcycle category.
q-6709: Correct answer: A. Category T entitles you to drive an agricultural tractor, also with a trailer. A tractor unit requires category C, and a quadricycle does not fall within the entitlements of category T.
q-6734: Correct answer: A. A sudden drop in blood sugar in a driver with diabetes causes weakness and impaired consciousness and can end in a sudden loss of consciousness at the wheel. Before driving, blood sugar is checked and a supply of carbohydrates is carried.
q-6759: Correct answer: B. If a driver works at night, their working time in a given 24-hour period may not exceed 10 hours. The limit covers not only driving but also loading, servicing the vehicle and other duties.
q-6760: Correct answer: B. The daily driving time is 9 hours as standard. It may be extended to 10 hours, but only on a limited number of days a week, so the unextended value remains 9 hours.
q-6761: Correct answer: C. Weekly driving time may not exceed 56 hours. In addition, the total driving time in two consecutive weeks is limited, so a maximum week must be followed by a shorter one.
q-6762: Correct answer: B. A regular daily rest period lasts at least 11 consecutive hours. It may be reduced only in a limited number of cases, and it is taken within the 24-hour period counted from the end of the previous rest.
q-6764: Correct answer: C. A regular weekly rest period lasts at least 45 consecutive hours. It must begin no later than after six 24-hour periods counted from the end of the previous weekly rest.
q-6765: Correct answer: B. A reduced weekly rest period lasts at least 24 consecutive hours. The reduction is an exception and requires the missing hours to be compensated later, attached to another rest period.
q-6766: Correct answer: B. Data from the driver card is downloaded no less often than every 28 days, so that the records are not overwritten and remain available for checks. Data from the digital tachograph is downloaded less often, but also at set intervals.
q-6767: Correct answer: A. Supervising loading is neither driving nor rest but other work, so the tachograph switch is set to the position meaning other work — in the material variant A corresponds to it. The wrong choice understates the recorded working time.
q-6768: Correct answer: C. A roadside check of a driver's working time may cover the current day and the 28 preceding days. The driver must have with them the record sheets, certificates and driver card documenting that whole period.
q-6769: Correct answer: B. A reduced daily rest period is at least 9 consecutive hours. It may be used at most three times between two weekly rest periods; the rule remains the longer rest.
q-6770: Correct answer: A. The daily driving time may be extended at most twice a week. On the other days the basic time applies, and exceeding the limit is a breach detected when the tachograph data is read.
q-6771: Correct answer: A. The driver must have with them documents covering the current day and the 28 preceding days. These are record sheets, driver card records and certificates of days off or of other work performed.
q-6772: Correct answer: A. Changing a wheel is an activity performed for the employer, so it counts as other work, not as a break or a period of availability. This time is recorded with the appropriate setting of the tachograph switch.
q-6811: Correct answer: B. The driver must have with them the working-time records for the recent period, and days without a tachograph record are confirmed by a certificate of the reasons for missing record sheets or not using the driver card. The licence is the operator's document, and the medical certificate concerns professional entitlements.
q-6815: Correct answer: A. A journey by a vehicle exceeding the permitted dimensions, mass or axle loads requires a permit of the appropriate category, which the driver carries and shows for a check. Voluntary insurance or the employer's consent does not make such a journey lawful.
q-6816: Correct answer: A. A category I permit is issued by the road authority responsible for the section along which the journey is to take place, because it is the one that assesses the load-bearing capacity of the surface and the engineering structures. The employer and the Police do not issue such permits.
q-6817: Correct answer: B. A vehicle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document, in which a valid technical inspection result is recorded. The driving licence concerns the driver's entitlements, and the consignment note the load carried, not the vehicle's legal status.
q-6853: Correct answer: C. A bus meeting the additional technical conditions may travel at up to 100 km/h on a road marked with the sign in the material. This is the highest speed provided for buses; higher values concern cars.
q-6865: Correct answer: A. In two consecutive weeks the total driving time may not exceed 90 hours. In a single week the limit is 56 hours, so after a maximum week correspondingly less remains for the next.
q-6868: Correct answer: A. A roadside check may cover the current day and the 28 previous days. That is why the driver must have with them the driver card and, if necessary, record sheets or printouts from that whole period.
q-6869: Correct answer: C. Data from the driver card is downloaded no less often than every 28 days. The card's memory is limited and once full the oldest records are overwritten, and the operator must keep full working-time records.
q-6870: Correct answer: B. Cleaning and washing the bus is an activity performed for the employer, so it counts as other work. It is neither a break, in which the driver freely disposes of their time, nor a period of availability.
q-6871: Correct answer: A. Keeping the bus clean is other work, so the tachograph switch is set to the position marked A in the material, corresponding to other work, not to rest or a period of availability.
q-6873: Correct answer: B. A regular daily rest period is at least 11 consecutive hours. It may be taken in two parts — a shorter one and then a longer one — and a reduced rest, no shorter than 9 hours, is allowed only a limited number of times.
q-6874: Correct answer: C. Compensation hours are taken in one go, in full, attached to another rest period lasting at least 9 hours. Splitting them into parts is not allowed, because it would not give the driver full recovery.
q-6875: Correct answer: B. A regular weekly rest lasts 45 hours, so after 35 hours have been taken, 10 hours remain to be taken. The compensation is taken in full, attached to another rest period.
q-6876: Correct answer: C. From the full weekly rest of 45 hours we subtract the 24 hours taken, which gives 21 hours of compensation. It must be taken in full, together with another rest period.
q-7079: Correct answer: A. In the dark the eye distinguishes shapes and contrasts less well, so an obstacle is recognised much later than in daylight. Well-chosen glasses and correct visual acuity make observation easier, not harder.
q-7102: Correct answer: C. Driving a tram requires a separate permit, issued after completing training and passing an examination and after medical checks confirming no contraindications. A category B or C driving licence gives no such entitlement.
q-7171: Correct answer: A. The person sitting at the controls of a towed motorcycle is still riding it, so they must hold the entitlement of the appropriate category. The type of connection — rigid or flexible — changes nothing here.
